boundary: Original CI packages, unchanged example C#/HTML source, isolated PackageReferences instead of ProjectReferences. Browser runtime rebuilt with the unchanged module builder and the ClientAssets producer referencing the original CI Composition package. No platform package rebuilt.

observations: Actual browser inspect/install succeeded using DotnetPluginToolchain, not an injected installation fixture.
Settings edit persisted limit 7 and advanced the live form revision from 0 to 1.
Disabling the provider removed panel contributions; enabling restored one contribution.
After client disposal and Host shutdown, a new process reacquired the profile and restored the active CLR plugin, limit 7 and one panel contribution. The new Settings owner reported revision 0.
Standard remove withdrew the plugin and retained deployment files. A second process restart did not reactivate it.

All temporary application Hosts were stopped with the normal Ctrl+C shutdown signal. The PowerShell PTY wrapper reported exit 1 from interruption; this is not a claim of a captured zero process exit code.

defaultDesktopOpening.observed: The real Settings action started Windows Explorer/OpenWith. The human confirmed a window appeared and closed it without choosing an editor.

ide.initialHumanObservation: EchoServiceTypert, RemoteService and RemoteMethod were unresolved on first opening.
ide.cause: The IDE inherited NUGET_PACKAGES and reused the published alpha.4 cache, overriding fixture NuGet.Config globalPackagesFolder. That package lacks the current Remote attributes, analyzer and build targets.
ide.fixtureCorrection: Set RestorePackagesPath in the isolated Directory.Build.props and preparation script; preserve the failed assets and global cache. No platform or published-package changes.
ide.correctedRestore: Rider automatically restored the original CI package hash and completed design-time build. A separate restore probe retained the conflicting environment and also selected the isolated cache.
ide.correctedEditorObservation: Human confirmed all three symbols resolved without manual build after correcting cache isolation.
ide.debugObservation: Human confirmed the breakpoint at Console.WriteLine(contribution.Package) was hit, then Example.Author and 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 were printed.

hmr.sample: One cold process running the unchanged packaged JintExpressionEvaluator through Context.RunAsync, followed by two warm evaluations and recovery.
hmr.boundary: Sampled stack durations overlap and must not be added. This probe did not reproduce the historical ten-second timeout or prove the cause of its whole twelve-second delay. Engine construction/Temporal timezone discovery is established for this sample, not inferred from a later green test. No production code, assertion, timeout, concurrency or retry changed.

dispositionRecommendation.status: Pending maintainer acceptance of a residual latency risk; not a proven environment failure or closed historical timeout.
dispositionRecommendation.recommendation: Retain current implementation, ten-second regression wait and failure evidence. Accept optional trusted-expression cold-preparation latency as a bounded release scope risk if the maintainer agrees; do not claim a measured upper latency bound.
dispositionRecommendation.observableImpact: Synchronous cold evaluator preparation delays the current serialized configuration refresh, subsequent coordinator work and disposal that drains that refresh. No new data-loss, missing-error or non-draining-owner defect was established.
dispositionRecommendation.limits: The Jint execution constraint is not an end-to-end deadline covering engine construction and native initialization. The new sample identifies one initialization path, not the complete historical delay.
reopenWhen: Queue progress, error publication or cleanup fails after evaluator completion.
A repeatable production scenario demonstrates unacceptable cold-preparation latency requiring a platform correction.
A hard total evaluation deadline becomes an approved product requirement.
notSelected: Increase timeout or weaken assertions to get green results.
Mandatory warmup that moves latency without bounding it.
Engine replacement or off-domain background evaluation without a proven behavioral need.

retainedPreparationFailures: Initial isolated Host added reflection-disabled serialization, unlike the source example; real installation refused after preparation. The override was removed and that profile/residual deployment preserved.
Retry into the preserved failed profile correctly refused an existing deployment directory; acceptance used a separately named profile.
A rebuild attempted before Host shutdown completed failed on a locked application output; the next build waited for shutdown and passed.
Diagnostic source initially used a nonexistent exception property; the corrected diagnostic uses the exception type. These are diagnostic/setup failures, not additional product regressions.
validationBoundary: No new Windows/Linux, upstream shard or AOT full gate. Original CI remains the production-source baseline. Rider 2026.2 symbol visibility and debugging passed with human observation after correcting the proven fixture package-cache mismatch. No Visual Studio or other IDE acceptance is claimed. Desktop editor content remains unverified; HMR historical-risk disposition remains open. A separate original-package compilation independently confirmed CS0122 for external ResultSchema access; this is a consumer boundary finding, not a failed full CI or a completed API correction.

runtimeExport.status: Existing public descriptor/STJ-based export through shared emitter and Connection; independent saved-model restrictions are not global Host restrictions.
runtimeExport.evidence: Repository ManagedApplication original-package consumption. Additional private-application success is an external thread report, not independently rerun here.

failureProjection.status: Fixed DSH and .NET both preserve explicit RemoteError fields and the message of ordinary exceptions under gateway/internal. No general safe-error policy or host-wide exception projection callback is established.
failureProjection.recommendation: Keep fixed behavior unless a host-wide policy is explicitly approved. Existing business boundaries can emit public-safe RemoteError values. A uniform policy request remains a release-scope decision, not a secretly implemented adaptation.

outputSchema.status: Concrete public export gap for consumers requiring the exact output-direction schema. Schema is public input projection; ResultSchema is internal. Generated Web type declarations do not provide complete runtime DTO validation.
outputSchema.recommendation: If required for alpha5 consumption, expose the existing read-only output-direction projection with its current lazy validation semantics. Do not use input Schema as output, reflection, copied DTO schemas or a new validator/model. API scope decision precedes implementation.
outputSchema.notEstablished: No result-schema API was added and no client validation behavior was changed.
outputSchema.probeWrapperNote: The initial wrapper expected CS1061; the compiler actually returned the more precise CS0122 protection-level diagnostic. The retained compiler log was checked directly without rerunning compilation.

consumerBoundaryReview.validation: Paired documentation check passed: 15 pairs, 9 package readmes. No production, API snapshot, dependency or version change; no repeated full gate.
